- new: autosave after each puzzle unlock, you can choose between your manual and the auto save when loading (so they are two separate savegames)

notes.title: Achievement fixes

You can now view the state of your achievements in the game under the stats in the main menu

[img]https://i.ibb.co/LNMXPdJ/local-Achievements.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Part 2 release date announcement
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/52669ed4b5830a7b9d7611ed94c7b72ce9758d6c.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

Almost 19 months ago, the first part of "Escape Room - The Sick Colleague" got released. I never imagined it to be so popular and only your positive feedback kicked off the development of part 2. Thank you for that! It feels like ages ago and I have to thank you for your patience in not knowing an exact release date. So today I am very happy to be able to tell you, that part 2 will be available the next week on the 6th of April! :)

My initial plan was to not only release the game but also two very minor DLCs you can spend money on if you want to support the game. However, I am still waiting for my new tax ID to arrive to be able to set a price for the DLCs on Steam. This has led to the situation for the last few days that I am not releasing a free game for which some of you have been waiting a long time for the reason of... money. And this seems ridiculous to me. So I won't delay it any longer and put the game out now and the DLCs a bit later.

I hope you like the new room and that it is in a state you can play without any major bugs. The testing team did a really good job of pointing things out that are fixed now before you have to suffer through them (if you want, come to the Discord and thank the testers for suffering for you :D). I also want to give a special thanks to Urwis12 and Abdullah Ali Waleed for not only testing a lot but also helping on the Discord and being very helpful in discussing issues regarding the game.

Not everything is finished though and there will be a few updates in the next weeks. Some translations are still missing and Spanish will be the next one to arrive. Also, the possibility to rebind the controls in-game is planned as a future update.

Like I said above, there will also be two very optional DLCs so nobody gets left behind regarding the main game. I will announce them later on but here is a short hint of what is planned for them:

[h3]Supporter DLC[/h3]
Here you can buy a highly decorative support sticker that will show up in-game. You can also print it out and put it on your jacket, you will be regarded as highly sympathetic at parties :)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/be9f0cc563fb8319a9e859d4835d7f2b81b358fc.gif[/img]

[h3]Character pack DLC[/h3]
For the multiplayer mode, this pack contains six new characters to choose from. They are all very intelligent so puzzle solving will be easier than ever :)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/0b44fb854978ebdbc5e6d6be191e981993559c4b.png[/img]


Thank you very much for your company on this journey! It has been stressful at times but also quite fulfilling. :)

notes.title: Download temporarily disabled
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/af50361884bd53643384e6651bb8e3c71e346e94.png[/img]

Dear players,

Today I have sad news for you. The download of the game will have to be disabled temporarily in the next few days.

The owners of the real-life escape room, on which "The Sick Colleague" is based, have contacted me and although they acknowledged the effort that went into the digital remake, they found it to be too similar. Therefore they have the rightful concern that someday someone might visit their real-life room knowing how to solve it already because of playing "The Sick Colleague".

Because of that, we agreed to disable the download until I have changed it to a significant amount or until their room gets decommissioned one day. Changing the room would mean a lot of work and my priorities lie with the second room at the moment (which is around 80% finished right now).

If you already downloaded and played the game you will still be able to do so. I will also keep the multiplayer servers up and running. I am sorry for the inconvenience this may cause you.

This event leaves me quite sad, but I hope to finish the second room soon so you can start escaping with your friends again in the near future. Thank you all for playing and the wonderful feedback so far!

notes.title: State of progress for part 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/3649d81a71e344fbc200c09e272ab969781bf769.png[/img]

Hi all,

Sorry for the long time without updates but things are getting slower than I wished for them to be. This is mostly caused by my lack of modeling skills that I am still developing. The new room has a lot more "complex" objects and I tend to make them more detailed than maybe necessary. But I think this is good for my personal development so I will stick with it for now.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/223d768bce39ed31ab270d27a322b47b7f13a623.png[/img]
Also, in my enthusiasm for modeling, I injured my arm and wasn't able to do anything for the whole month. :( At least I can say that a part of the room is almost finished so I am thinking about putting it on a beta branch so some of you may test it out and look for bad puzzle design.

In other news, I got in contact with the great devs from Pine Studio. They are also developing an escape room game and we had a few good chats about the problems we are facing. Definitely feels good being able to cooperate with someone. They were kind enough to send me their game to check it out and I have to say it is looking really great. It has some similar features as The Sick Colleague like being able to move and throw (and break!) most objects in the room. You can play it in co-op as well and the biggest feature for me is a level editor where you can create your own rooms and share them in the Steam workshop!
Since some of you asked me about that for my game, which right now I am not able to do because I still have to learn how to do that, I think this might be interesting for you. They have a demo version so please hop over to their page and check it out and put it on your wishlist if you like it. That would help them a lot! :)
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1435790?utm_source=1301720_steam

That's it for now, thank you for staying patient, I am hoping to be back with more news soon!

notes.title: About part 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/2d9493fa9c2a80fda3d034df3a3d6c2a6cef6683.png[/img]

Hi all,

Today I am not writing about some bug fix or improvement on the game but about the progress on the second part of the game since many of you said they would play it rather sooner than later :)
We are on the same page here, I would like to finish it as soon as possible while making sure the quality is the best I can do. The whole process takes longer as you might expect because like I already told on the Discord I have a day job to pay the bills and to keep the game free for everyone. That means programming more or less 8h and after that working on the game. Sadly this is not possible every day because often the job takes most of my brain energy away. So thinking about some clever puzzles was taking sooo long in the last weeks. I am planning to reduce my working hours from 40 to 30 per week to be able to focus a bit more on the game. I hope you are able to stay patient and understand the situation ;)

Now to the information: part two is planned to be included in this game so you can choose which part you want to play and no other download in Steam will be needed. It will continue the story of part one and the concept with all puzzles and flow of the game are finished right now. At the moment I am making some placeholder objects in Blender to build the room as a crude prototype so I can walk around in the room and see if everything checks out and if the puzzles make sense. So I might go back and change a few things until it feels right.

After that, I will start modeling the objects in a detailed way and build one section after the other. Hopefully, this will go faster because it takes a different "energy" from me and I even find it relaxing. Some programming will be needed to make new types of puzzles possible but much of the code from part one can be reused. I am thinking about making some beta versions available once a section is finished to get some feedback from some players because part one had a few issues that were unclear. If you work too long on one thing you can't see those issues for yourself. Let's see, I will give updates about that on the Discord and here as well.

In other news: I contacted Steam about the game having limited profile features (e.g. achievements not showing in your profile etc.) and they had a look and decided to remove that limitation. Thanks to Alden Kroll from Steam for that!

Some improvements for the game are also planned when I find the time. For example, I'd like to add Steam cloud saves and name tags on the players in multiplayer so you can easily call out the right friend for making shenanigans :D

That's it for today, have a nice weekend, I hope to have new updates soon. Let me know if you are interested in that kind of update from our journey to part two!

notes.title: Saving is now enhanced
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/dd68c9fb5884e19346f61fd4c7487a1b3c18c2df.png[/img]

Hi all,

This update enhances the saving and loading capabilities a lot. So far, only the state of the locks got saved but from now on the position and state of almost everything is stored. That way, you can save your beautiful artworks you created with the items (post a screenshot!) or even the mess you leave behind :D
Your old saves are still functional and get converted the next time you save.

You can save and load anytime during the game and the best part is, it works in multiplayer as well. If you load a game, every player gets the same state. This can also be used to update the room for everyone should items run out of sync (e.g. a door is open for one player and not for the other). The room state is also synced to everyone at the start of a multiplayer game so for example, you can play the game alone for some time then invite some friends and continue together. If you find any issues let me know, I am sure there are some scenarios that can cause new glitches.

Additional to that there were a few other small improvements listed below. I hope this helps you in your escapes!


- two players grabbing an item at the same time should result in the item dropping on the floor so it won't get stuck in your hands
- ask if you want to save on quitting the game
- no more object preview when you can interact with an item
- added some hints in the UI, how to join a room, using F10 etc.
- show last changes in the main menu when hovering over the version number
- fixed rotating of objects (hold R)
- fixed the vase ;)
- fixed the reset of certain objects when using F11 to reset everything
- fixed some colliders

notes.title: It's the litte things...
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/eac562c81af0645f3e3cad49727d44f66e653d68.png[/img]

Hi all,

Update 1.17 has a few adjustments in store:

- there is a second high score list for players who play for the first time and finish in a "normal" time. So they should not get drowned in the mass of speedrunners. Those can continue to battle for rankings in the old list. I know, would have been nice to have this from the start but some things seem obvious only in hindsight.

- the new hotkey F10 can be used anytime now to deactivate the automatic controller detection. There were some cases where broken controllers, flight sticks/HOTAS, or 3D mice were sending input that the game recognized as a controller. So if your mouse cursor disappears in the menu or you are running in circles in the game, just press F10 and see if that helps.

- the help system ist more robust now so you should not receive hints for puzzles that you already solved

- in the main menu there is a new button above the version number showing some (very useful) statistics. To be honest, I just wanted to try out the statistics system of Steam :D so right now you can only see how many games were played or finished by you or all players but maybe it will see some additions later like traveled distance, thrown objects, etc. What would you like to see there?

- movement in the multiplayer mode should now be more smooth due to a higher update rate

- the clock is synced to all clients in multiplayer mode so all players will have the same time at the end no matter when they joined the game. The mysterious 0 seconds high score should be a matter of the past now (at least coming from that glitch, I am sure you will be creative to find other ways :)

Have fun!

notes.title: Arabic language version released
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37742201/16581c04aea4292651933e81fbcb43328ce05f16.png[/img]

Hi all,

This update adds the Arabic language option to the game. Why Arabic?

The wonderful Abdulrahman Fayez (Abdulrahman388 on Steam) offered his help to translate the game into his mother tongue and I can't thank him enough for that!

Also, Arabic is spoken by around 300 million people natively and by that is the fifth most spoken language in the world. Usually, if you look up the languages you should have a translation for, Arabic is not mentioned. I guess because the "market" does not generate enough "revenue". And that is fine, the money has to come back in. But since this game is free to play anyway and the translation was also for free, it is really great to make it available to such a large group of people.

The technical challenges to put Arabic into the game were surprisingly cumbersome because Unity has no native support for right-to-left languages. So with all the struggles, I expect there to be a few (a lot?) errors in the text because I could just make a rough visual comparison. If you find any mistakes please don't blame Abdulrahman but me and report them here or in the Discord and I will try to fix them as soon as possible. :)
